name: Ndengeleko
catalog_citation: Ström, Eva-Marie. 2013. The Ndengeleko Language of Tanzania. PhD dissertation, University of Gothenburg (GUPEA 2077/32111).
catalog_locator: ch. 4: §4.2 Long vowels (pp. 96-97); §4.4 Syllable structure (pp. 101-104, tone passage pp. 103-104)
catalog_quote: In Bantu languages, divergences in surface pitch can be understood in terms of the distribution of ‘primary’ High tones and their surface modifications (Kisseberth and Odden 2003:59). There is as yet no analysis of the distribution of tones in Ndengeleko. Partial reduction of tonal distinctions for the whole of the P10 group was indicated by Guthrie (1967 p.56, p.69). Odden (1996:3) includes a brief analysis of Ndengeleko tone and concludes that possible contrasts in the position of H tone are highly limited. Surface high pitched syllables have been marked with an acute accent in this work. Following the definition by Hyman (2001): ‘A language with tone is one in which an indication of pitch enters into the lexical realisation of at least some morphemes’, I conclude that this holds for Ndengeleko. Due to time constraints, however, it has not been possible to provide a complete analysis …

audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: The record rests on the only reference grammar of the language (Ström 2013, 302 pp, open-access PhD), which we hold; the deciding quotation and the domain quote are verbatim at the stated pages (pp.103-104, p.96, p.101). The grammar explicitly calls Ndengeleko a tone language, marks surface H, gives no word-stress or accent rule, and denies penultimate lengthening because the vowel-length contrast is retained, so 'tonal' (tonal-OR-pitch accent, domain not stated by the source) follows directly. No better or later prosodic study exists per Glottolog and web search; the only additional material is Odden's brief second-hand treatments (1996:3; 2003 handbook chapter), which could refine the note on how restricted the H system is but would not move the language out of the tonal/pitch accent class. The one open item downloaded now (Ström 2009 ACAL) is silent on prosody. No identity problem: Rufiji is not a separ
